# CurlCustomHeadWithoutNoBody

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Setting a custom HEAD method does not configure all of cURL's transfer behavior. Use the no-body option for a HEAD transfer.

## Example

```php{2,3}
<?php
$h=curl_init();curl_setopt($h,CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST,"HEAD");curl_exec($h);
$other=curl_init();curl_setopt($other,CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST,"HEAD");curl_setopt($other,CURLOPT_NOBODY,false);curl_exec($other);
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Use CURLOPT_NOBODY for a HEAD transfer.</li>
<li>line 3: Use CURLOPT_NOBODY for a HEAD transfer.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- Resolved curl handle final CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST is literal HEAD and CURLOPT_NOBODY is definitely false/default before curl_exec. Require handle local ownership and no unknown configuration calls.
- Account for a later CURLOPT_HTTPGET setter resetting no-body transfer behavior. The finding must describe the final mode rather than an earlier explicit CURLOPT_NOBODY value.
- D1f. Local ownership requires an uncopied handle allocation. Before the reported `curl_exec`, the handle variable may only appear as a direct call argument, as the target of a plain assignment, or in a boolean test (`if`/`elseif` condition, `!`, `isset`, `empty`, `==`, `!=`, `===`, `!==`, `&&`, `||`). Copying it into another binding loses the shared option proof. Uses after the reported call do not matter.
- Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods; user-defined lookalikes are excluded. Follow only bounded local proof in one lexical scope.
- Emit one finding per violating operation, not per supporting evidence statement. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Do not report unresolved or shadowed builtin names, unknown values, or incomplete receiver/type provenance. Unknown calls, aliases escaping, and intervening writes invalidate local proof. Similar code outside the stated detection contract is not a finding.
- Do not report when the handle or a copy of it leaves the D1f positions before the call, because code the rule cannot follow may then configure it: capture in a closure `use` list, mention inside an arrow function, array literal item (including one passed as an argument), store into a property, array element or static property, reference binding, variable-variable access in the same scope, a `compact()` or `get_defined_vars()` call in the same scope, or any other value position such as `@$h`, `$h ?: $x` or `$h ?? $x`.
- Both standard suppression forms suppress this native ID.

## Fix

None. Choosing a repair requires intent or additional runtime information.

## PHP versions

Available throughout supported PHP 5.3–8.5 where the referenced builtin/extension is available. Respect syntax/version-specific receiver contracts; unavailable APIs are not this rule’s concern.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "CurlCustomHeadWithoutNoBody": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore CurlCustomHeadWithoutNoBody
```
